match.reason: No point in the bank covers choosing between leading-edge and established technology; the closest one, on technological influences, is about technology as an outside force on a business, not about a business choosing which technology to use.

draft.title: Technology choices
card: Operations managers choose what technology the business uses to make goods or deliver services. The choice is between leading-edge and established technology.
the newest technology available. It usually costs more and is less tested, but it may give the business an advantage over competitors.
technology that is already proven and widely used. It usually costs less and is more reliable, but it is unlikely to set a business apart from rivals.
A business weighs its budget, its need to stand out and the risk of untested technology. Neither choice is right for every business.
draft.remember: Leading-edge costs more and may give an advantage. Established is proven and cheaper.

a.q: Which statement best describes leading-edge technology?
opts: It is the newest available and may give an advantage
It is widely used and has a long record of reliability
It is cheaper to buy but gives no chance of an advantage
It is the technology that competitors already use
a.why: Leading-edge technology is the newest available. It costs more and is less tested, but it may set a business apart. The option about a long record describes established technology.
a.clue: Think about which type is newest and least tested.

b.q: Priya runs a small bakery in Bathurst with a tight budget. She needs dependable ovens and has no plan to stand out through new equipment. Which choice suits her best?
opts: Established ovens, because they are proven and cheaper
Leading-edge ovens, because they are always more productive
Leading-edge ovens, because they are cheaper to run
Established ovens, because they beat rivals on new features
b.why: Priya has a tight budget and wants dependability, so proven and cheaper established ovens fit. Leading-edge ovens may give an advantage, but they cost more and are less tested, so they do not match her needs.
b.clue: Match her budget and need for dependability to the type of technology.

a.best: It is the newest available and may give an advantage

b.best: Established ovens, because they are proven and cheaper

The distractor 'Leading-edge ovens, because they are always more productive' uses 'always', which the card never claims. This makes it easy to eliminate without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Technology choices
card: Operations managers choose what technology the business uses to make goods or deliver services. The choice is between leading-edge and established technology.
the newest technology available. It usually costs more and is less tested, but it may give the business an advantage over competitors.
technology that is already proven and widely used. It usually costs less and is more reliable, but it is unlikely to set a business apart from rivals.
A business weighs its budget, its need to stand out and the risk of untested technology. Neither choice is right for every business.
proposal.remember: Leading-edge costs more and may give an advantage. Established is proven and cheaper.

a.q: What trade-off does a business accept when it chooses leading-edge technology?
opts: Higher cost and risk, for a possible edge over rivals
Lower cost and risk, for a possible edge over rivals
Higher cost and risk, for a likely gain in reliability
Lower cost and risk, for less chance to stand out
a.why: Leading-edge technology usually costs more and is less tested, but it may set a business apart from rivals. Greater reliability is not the gain: proven, established technology is the more reliable choice.
a.clue: Think about what the business gives up and what it hopes to gain.

b.q: Priya runs a small bakery in Bathurst with a tight budget. She needs dependable ovens and has no plan to stand out through new equipment. Which choice suits her best?
opts: Established ovens, because they are proven and cheaper
Leading-edge ovens, because they may help her stand out
Leading-edge ovens, because they are the most reliable
Established ovens, because they set her apart from rivals
b.why: Priya has a tight budget and wants dependability, so proven, cheaper established ovens fit her needs. Leading-edge ovens may help a business stand out, but Priya has no plan to compete that way, and they cost more and are less tested.
b.clue: Which benefits does Priya need, and which does she not need?

a.best: Higher cost and risk, for a possible edge over rivals

b.best: Established ovens, because they are proven and cheaper
